## 1.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 1.] The purpose of the early notification letter is twofold. First, the intention is to give defendants and their insurers as much advance warning as possible about the possibility of a claim so that they can begin to investigate the matter. This is particularly so where relevant information may be decades old and may take time to locate and retrieve. Second, where the claimant has severely limited life expectancy it gives advance warning to defendants of the need for urgency in locating relevant information.

## 2.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 2.] It is intended that the early notification letter will be sent before the letter of claim and will not start the timetable for response as set out in paragraph 7 of this protocol.

## 3.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 3.] As soon as sufficient information is available to identify a proposed defendant, the claimant should send to the proposed defendant two copies of the early notification letter. One copy is for the defendant, the second for passing on to the defendant’s insurers. The claimant should also send a further copy of the same letter directly to the defendant’s insurer, where known. In the case of a defunct company the further copy of the letter should be sent to the relevant insurer or handler of that defunct company.

## Content of Early Notification Letter

## 4.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 4.] All copies of the early notification letter should be clearly marked ‘MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM’.

## 5.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 5.] The early notification letter should contain basic information sufficient to identify the claimant, the periods of relevant exposure and the potential defendants. As a minimum, the early notification letter should contain the following information:

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 5.] (a) name and address of the claimant/deceased;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 5.] (b) national insurance number of the claimant/deceased (if known);

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 5.] (c) claimant/deceased’s date of birth;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 5.] (d) employers, where known, of relevant employment and or exposure;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 5.] (e) occupiers of premises, where known, of relevant employment and/or exposure;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 5.] (f) date or approximate dates, where known, of relevant employment and or exposure;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 5.] (g) direct contact details, including e-mail address, for the claimant’s legal representative;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 5.] (h) marital status;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 5.] (i) details of dependents; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 5.] (j) date of diagnosis.

## 6.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 6.] Solicitors are recommended to use a standard format for the early notification letter. An example is set out in Annex D. This can be amended to suit the particular case.

## 7.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 7.] The early notification letter should indicate whether a claim is also being made against any other potential defendant and identify any known insurer involved.

## 8.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 8.] The early notification letter is not intended to have the same status as a statement of case in proceedings. Matters may come to light as a result of investigation after the letter of claim has been sent.

## Employment and Exposure History

## 9.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 9.] In view of the joint and several liability provided for in the Compensation Act 2006 in mesothelioma cases the information set out in paragraph 6.5 of this protocol is particularly relevant.

## Defendant’s response

## 10.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 10.] The defendant should respond within 14 days of the date of the letter confirming that the matter is receiving urgent attention.

## Compliance with this protocol

## 11.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > 11.] Attention is drawn to paragraph 9.1 of Practice Direction 3D (Mesothelioma Claims) which provides that in Living Mesothelioma Claims (normally where the claimant has severely limited life expectancy) strict adherence to this protocol may not be required. The issue of compliance with this protocol in relation to certain mesothelioma claims is also recognised at paragraph 2.7 of this protocol.

## Annex D EARLY NOTIFICATION LETTER FOR USE IN CASES INVOLVING MESOTHELIOMA

## URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] YOU MUST DEAL WITH THIS LETTER IMMEDIATELY

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] Dear Sirs,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] We are acting on behalf of the above-named who has developed mesothelioma. We are investigating whether this disease may have been caused:

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] during the course of his employment with you / name of employer if different whilst at your premises at (address)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] between the approximate dates of: (insert relevant dates of employment/at the premises)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] as a result of your product (name)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] Please note your insurers will require you to advise them of this letter. You must pass a copy of this letter to your insurer immediately.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] We are writing this letter in accordance with the Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] Our client’s details are as follows:

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] Name:

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] Address:

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] National Insurance Number (if known):

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] Date of Birth:

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] Marital status:

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] Details of dependents:

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] Date of diagnosis.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] We require a response from you confirming this matter is receiving urgent attention within 14 days of the date of this letter.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] The direct e-mail address, which you may use for urgent communications and which should be followed up with paper copies, is: (insert e-mail address)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > URGENT – MESOTHELIOMA CLAIM] Yours faithfully

## Annex E

## NOISE INDUCED HEARING LOSS CLAIMS MADE ON OR AFTER 1ST OCTOBER 2023

## General

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > General] E1. This Annex sets out the procedure to be adopted for those claims for noise induced hearing loss (NIHL) which are likely to be suitable for allocation to the fast track. The procedure is intended to support the regime for fixed recoverable costs for such claims set out in Section VIII of Part 45.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > General] E2. This Annex supplements the general provisions of this Protocol and applies to NIHL claims where the first letter of claim is sent on or after 1st October 2023. Where there is a difference between the general provisions and the contents of this Annex, the provisions in this Annex take precedence.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > General] E3. Annex E has been created following the final report of the CJC working party in 2017 (https://www.judiciary.uk/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/fixed-costs-in-noise-induced-hearing-loss-claims-20170906.pdf). Practitioners may find the discussion in that report provides helpful background, although it should not be used as an aid to interpretation of this Annex.

## Exclusions

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Exclusions] E4. The following types of NIHL claim are excluded from the fixed recoverable costs regime—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Exclusions] (a)  military claims, i.e. claims by members of the armed forces in respect of their service career;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Exclusions] (b)  claims valued at more than £25,000;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Exclusions] (c)  claims allocated to or likely to be suitable for the intermediate track or the multi-track;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Exclusions] (d)  claims properly brought against 4 or more defendants, each of which is either still trading or has identified insurance cover for the material period;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Exclusions] (e)  claims where any defendant in their letter of response—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Exclusions] (i)    alleges that the claimant’s occupational hearing loss is de minimis;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Exclusions] (ii)    requests a second audiogram;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Exclusions] (iii)    requests their own medical evidence;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Exclusions] (f) any claim considered to be a test case on issues of breach of duty in respect of any defendant;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Exclusions] (g)  claims against sole defendants as set out in paragraphs E5 to E7 below.

## Claims against sole defendants

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Claims against sole defendants] E5. The Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims (“the EL/PL Protocol”) applies to a disease claim brought against a sole defendant, where that defendant appears on the list maintained by Claims Portal Ltd. (“the NIHL List”) for the purposes of this paragraph.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Claims against sole defendants] E6. A defendant may be entered by Claims Portal Ltd on the NIHL List—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Claims against sole defendants] (a)  where the defendant is still trading; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Claims against sole defendants] (b)  where the defendant is no longer trading, all relevant insurers have agreed to the defendant’s name being entered on the list.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Claims against sole defendants] E7. The effect of the defendant’s name being entered on the NIHL List is that all claims against that defendant as sole defendant must start in the EL/PL Protocol rather than under this Annex of this Protocol.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Claims against sole defendants] E8. Where the defendant’s name has not been entered on the NIHL List at the date when the letter of claim is sent, a claim against that defendant as sole defendant must be started in accordance with this Annex of this Protocol.

## NIHL letter of claim

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of claim] E9. The claimant must use the new format of the letter of claim at appendix 1, which is intended to provide more meaningful and relevant information. Proper use of this template should avoid the need for defendants to make requests for further information and should enable defendants to make early decisions on breach and to consider limitation and causation. This in turn should lead to costs savings and early filtering of and settlement of meritorious claims.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of claim] E10. The NIHL letter of claim must be accompanied by—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of claim] (a)  an audiogram produced by a suitably experienced and approved provider;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of claim] (b)  a schedule of the claimant’s employment from HMRC;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of claim] (c)  the search results from ELTO.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of claim] E11. The audiogram should be from an acceptable UK “quality standard” audiologist and from tests conducted in acceptable conditions. Provision of a sufficiently robust independent audiogram with the letter of claim is essential, as it enables the defendants to have some certainty that there is a diagnosis of NIHL which merits detailed investigation.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of claim] E12. Production of the HMRC schedule with the letter of claim should ensure that the claimant provides a more accurate working history, as well as offering independent validation of the claimant’s employment by the defendants.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of claim] E13. Where compliance with the procedure in this Annex is not possible before the expiry of the limitation period the claimant may start proceedings and apply to the court for an order to stay the proceedings while the parties take steps to follow this Annex.

## NIHL letter of response

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of response] E14. The defendants must use the new format of the letter of response in Appendix 2, which is intended to encourage defendants to make early admissions of breach of duty where they can do so and to narrow the areas of dispute. Use of the NIHL letter of claim, to include a better working history and disclosure of a suitable audiogram, should make it easier for defendants to conduct meaningful investigations and form a reasoned position on the issues in the claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of response] E15. The NIHL letter of response should address the issues fully, including identifying whether delegated authority applies (if relevant) under the ABI’s Claims Handling Guidelines and the name and reference for the coordinating insurer. Where there are multiple defendants, they should try to coordinate their positions at an early stage and to provide a coordinated response to the claimant where possible.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of response] E16. Where breach is denied, the defendants must disclose any noise surveys and other relevant documents with the letter of response. The defendants should also state whether their records reveal any previous claims brought by the claimant.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of response] E17. Use of requests for further information is discouraged. Defendants should consider all information provided in the NIHL letter of claim and only make a request if there is any material information missing.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of response] E18. The information provided in the NIHL letter of claim should allow defendants to make decisions on breach of duty and to consider limitation and causation, prior to receiving any further medical evidence. Defendants are therefore discouraged from making any offer of settlement prior to receipt of full medical evidence, save that they may respond to any offer of settlement made by the claimant prior to the letter of response.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > NIHL letter of response] E19. Where the claimant indicates in the letter of claim an intention to obtain full medical evidence, i.e. a full audiologist’s report or a report from an ENT surgeon, the defendants should normally agree that the time period for accepting any pre-medical offer should not start to run until that medical evidence is sent to the defendant.

## Medical evidence

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Medical evidence] E20. The provisions of this Protocol apply to medical evidence obtained under paragraphs E21 to E22 below. For the avoidance of doubt, the medical evidence contemplated in these paragraphs is in addition to the audiogram to be disclosed with the NIHL letter of claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Medical evidence] E21. Where liability is disputed, it is expected that the claimant will obtain and disclose medical evidence from an ENT specialist doctor.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Medical evidence] E22. Where liability is not in dispute, the claimant should obtain and disclose a medical report from an independent audiologist. In such cases a report from an ENT specialist will not normally be necessary. Any request by a defendant for a second audiogram in such cases is strongly discouraged.

## Costs stages

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Costs stages] E23. The pre-issue stages identified for the purposes of the fixed recoverable costs regime in Section VIII of Part 45 are as follows—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Costs stages] Stage 1 – up to and including sending the NIHL letter of claim and accompanying documents;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Costs stages] Stage 2A – cases where liability is admitted in the NIHL letter of response;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Costs stages] Stage 3A – cases where liability is not admitted in the NIHL letter of response;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Costs stages] Stage 2B/3B – as for 2A/3A above, plus an additional allowance for the cost of preparing papers to issue where incurred, whether by solicitors or counsel.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims > Costs stages] Appendix 1
